items.followUp: Explain the difference between an organism and a population.

rubric.why: A population consists of members of one species living in a particular area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying organisms as the same species and 1 mark for stating that they live in the same area.

rubric.why: A community is made up of populations of different species that live and interact in an area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying populations of different species and 1 mark for mentioning their shared area or interactions.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in a particular area at the same time.
A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.
Population and community are levels of biological organization above the individual organism.
A community includes all the populations present in its area.

items.followUp: Describe the process by which a cell releases a substance using a vesicle.

rubric.why: Endocytosis brings material into the cell by forming a vesicle from the plasma membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the membrane folding around or engulfing material and 1 mark for the resulting vesicle entering the cell.

rubric.why: Exocytosis releases material when an intracellular vesicle joins the plasma membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for vesicle fusion with the plasma membrane and 1 mark for release of contents outside the cell.

rubric.why: The labelled diagram should distinguish the inward movement of endocytosis from the outward release of exocytosis.
rubric.description: Provides a labelled diagram showing both processes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear diagram with the cell membrane, vesicle/material and correctly indicated directions.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the uptake of material into a cell by the plasma membrane.
The plasma membrane folds inward around the material and pinches off to form a vesicle inside the cell.
Exocytosis is the release of material from a cell when an intracellular vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane.
The vesicle empties its contents outside the cell.
Diagram: draw and label the cell boundary as the plasma membrane and label the inside as cytoplasm.
For endocytosis, show the plasma membrane folding inward around material and forming an intracellular vesicle; add an inward arrow.
For exocytosis, show a vesicle inside the cell fusing with the plasma membrane and releasing material outside; add an outward arrow.

items.followUp: Compare the lock and key and induced fit models of enzyme action.

rubric.why: The lock and key model explains enzyme specificity through a fixed active site that matches its substrate.
rubric.description: Explains the lock and key model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the active site has a fixed or specific shape and 1 mark for explaining that only a complementary substrate fits.

rubric.why: The induced fit model describes an active site that changes shape as the substrate binds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the active site is flexible or changes shape and 1 mark for explaining that substrate binding produces a better fit.

modelAnswer: In the lock and key model, an enzyme has a rigid active site with a particular shape.
Only a substrate with a complementary shape fits into the active site, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
In the induced fit model, the active site is flexible rather than completely rigid.
When the substrate binds, the active site changes shape to fit it more closely and catalyse the reaction.

items.followUp: Describe how anaerobic respiration in yeast is used in baking and brewing.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration allows cells to release energy when oxygen is unavailable.
rubric.description: States the basic role of anaerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking respiration without oxygen to the release of energy.

rubric.why: Yeast fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Identifies the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide as products.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide produced by yeast makes bread dough rise.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting carbon dioxide production with rising dough or bread-making.

rubric.why: The ethanol produced by yeast is used in brewing alcoholic drinks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting ethanol or alcohol production with brewing.

rubric.why: Muscle cells can respire anaerobically when their oxygen supply is insufficient, producing lactic acid and energy.
rubric.description: States the importance in muscle cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking insufficient oxygen in muscles with anaerobic respiration and lactic acid production.

modelAnswer: Anaerobic respiration releases energy in cells when oxygen is unavailable or insufficient.
In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
The carbon dioxide released by yeast makes bread dough rise during baking.
The ethanol produced by yeast is used in brewing alcoholic drinks.
Muscle cells can respire anaerobically when their oxygen supply is insufficient; lactic acid is produced and energy is released.

items.followUp: Define morphology and explain what it studies.

rubric.why: Physiology is concerned with the functions and processes of living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that physiology studies functions or how organisms work.

rubric.why: Anatomy is concerned with the structure of organisms and their parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that anatomy studies the structure or form of organisms.

modelAnswer: Physiology is the study of the functions and processes of living organisms.
Anatomy is the study of the structure and parts of living organisms.

items.followUp: What is a population? Give one example of a population in an ecosystem.

rubric.why: A population is made up of organisms belonging to the same species in a defined area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including organisms of the same species living in the same area.

rubric.why: A community includes populations of different species living and interacting in a shared area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including populations of different species in a shared area or their interactions.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in a particular area.
A community is all the populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

items.followUp: State two effects of deforestation on the environment.

rubric.why: Deforestation means the removal or clearing of forest cover.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the clearing or removal of forests or trees.

rubric.why: Common causes include clearing land for farming, obtaining timber or fuel, urban development, road construction and fires.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving one valid cause.

modelAnswer: Deforestation is the removal or clearing of forests, usually by cutting down trees.
Its causes include clearing land for agriculture, obtaining timber or fuel, urbanization, road construction and forest fires.

items.followUp: What is the main difference between organisms of kingdom Monera and those of kingdom Protista?

rubric.why: Monerans are unicellular organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Monerans are unicellular.

rubric.why: Monerans are prokaryotic and lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Monerans are prokaryotic or lack a membrane-bound nucleus or organelles.

modelAnswer: Organisms of kingdom Monera are unicellular.
They are prokaryotic and lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
